Transverse section of a young dicotyledonous stem (sunflower), drawn as a circle, with one sector enlarged on the right to show the cells in detail. Whole view: epidermis, cortex, a single ring of about eight wedge-shaped vascular bundles near the outside, medullary rays between them, and a large central pith. Enlarged sector: epidermis with cuticle and a multicellular hair; three layers of collenchyma (cells with thickened corners) forming the hypodermis; parenchyma cortex; wavy endodermis (starch sheath) with dark starch grains; a cap of thick-walled sclerenchyma (pericycle fibres) over the bundle; phloem; a thin band of cambium; xylem with large vessels on the outer side and small protoxylem towards the centre; a medullary ray; pith cells. Colours: xylem pale red, phloem pale blue, cambium pale green, sclerenchyma darker pink, cortex and pith pale cream.

Transverse section of a young monocotyledonous stem (maize), drawn as a circle, with one vascular bundle enlarged in a box on the right. Whole view: epidermis; two or three layers of thick-walled sclerenchyma hypodermis; ground tissue of parenchyma filling the whole stem; many scattered oval vascular bundles, small and crowded near the edge, larger and fewer towards the centre; no ring, no pith. Enlarged bundle: an oval sheath of thick-walled sclerenchyma; phloem (sieve tubes and companion cells) at the top (outer side); two large metaxylem vessels side by side; one or two small protoxylem vessels below them; a large round air space (protoxylem lacuna) at the bottom, giving the face-like appearance. Colours: xylem pale red, phloem pale blue, sclerenchyma darker pink, parenchyma pale cream.

Four panels side by side comparing plant supporting tissues. Panel 1, collenchyma: a transverse view of a few polygonal living cells with nuclei and walls thickened only at the corners (shown as bright pale-green thick corners), plus a small longitudinal view of elongated cells. Panel 2, sclerenchyma: a transverse view of thick-walled cells with very small empty centres and pit canals, plus a longitudinal view of long fibres with pointed overlapping ends and one small round sclereid (stone cell). Panel 3, xylem: a longitudinal view of four vessels showing annular, spiral, scalariform and pitted thickening, with no cross walls. Panel 4, phloem: a longitudinal view of a sieve tube with a sieve plate, a companion cell with nucleus, and a strand of long pointed phloem fibres beside them. Lignified walls in pink-red, cellulose walls in pale green.

Three simple transverse-section outlines side by side, showing where the supporting tissues are, using a colour key. 1) Dicot root: a circle with a central star of xylem coloured red, and a thin brown endodermis ring. 2) Dicot stem: a circle with a thin green ring of collenchyma just under the edge, small pink caps of sclerenchyma fibres over a ring of bundles with red xylem, and a pale pith. 3) Dicot leaf: a thin flat section with a thickened midrib containing green collenchyma patches above and below a vascular bundle with red xylem, and small red veins along the blade. A colour key at the bottom: green = collenchyma, pink = sclerenchyma / fibres, red = xylem.

Ventral view of a dissected rat lying on its back on a dissecting board, limbs pinned out, skin and body wall pinned back, rib cage removed. Thorax: heart in the middle with pink lungs on each side, trachea running up the neck, thymus over the heart. A thin diaphragm line separating thorax and abdomen. Abdomen: large dark red-brown lobed liver just behind the diaphragm; stomach on the animal's left (viewer's right) partly under the liver; dark red spleen beside the stomach; coiled small intestine; a large caecum; colon and rectum running to the anus; urinary bladder at the hind end; one kidney visible on each side where the gut is pushed aside. Natural soft colours.

Front view outline of a human torso (gender-neutral) showing the positions of the main internal organs as simple soft-coloured shapes. Chest: two lungs, heart between them tilted to the left, trachea above. Diaphragm as a curved line. Abdomen: large liver on the upper right of the body (viewer's left) with the small gall bladder beneath it; stomach on the upper left (viewer's right); spleen behind and left of the stomach; pancreas partly visible behind the stomach; coiled small intestine in the middle; large intestine framing it (caecum and appendix lower right of the body, colon around, rectum); bladder low in the pelvis. Show the two kidneys as dotted outlines behind the gut.

Male reproductive and urinary organs of a mammal (rabbit), ventral view, as a practical drawing. Show the bladder in the centre; the two ureters entering it from the kidneys above (kidneys partly shown); two oval testes in scrotal sacs on either side of the penis at the bottom; the coiled epididymis on each testis; the two sperm ducts (vas deferens) running up through the inguinal canals, looping over the ureters and joining the urethra behind the bladder; the seminal vesicle and prostate gland near this junction; small Cowper's glands lower down; the urethra running through the penis.
